response.title: which power station runs an aquarium the longest in a power outage
response.answer:
For keeping an aquarium running during a power outage, the best portable power station is one with a large LiFePO₄ battery, high usable capacity, and expandable battery storage.

The most important factor is battery capacity (Wh), not the advertised output power (W).

For example, a 4,000Wh power station can potentially keep a small aquarium's filtration and air pump running for several days, but a heater can drain that same battery in less than a day.

Here are the models I'd consider, along with estimated aquarium runtimes.

For most aquariums, prioritize running the air pump and filter. Turn off unnecessary lighting and other nonessential equipment. Heating can be the biggest power drain, so monitor water temperature and avoid abrupt changes rather than automatically disconnecting a heater.

For an unattended aquarium, also check the power station's automatic switchover behavior and test whether the filter reliably restarts after an outage.

## Calculate your aquarium's backup runtime

Adjust the wattage to see how long each power station could run your aquarium.

{@body const [watts,setWatts] = DIL.useState(25)}
{@body const stations = [{name:"Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus",wh:5040},{name:"EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3",wh:4096},{name:"Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus",wh:3840}]}
{@body const hours = wh => wh*0.85/watts}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **Total aquarium power consumption**
    <title size="lg" color="default" tabularNums>{watts}W</title>
  </row>
  <slider min={5} max={300} step={5} value={watts} onChange={setWatts}/>

    <text color="secondary" size="xs">5W · Air pump</text>

      <row justify="between" align="center">
        <text weight="medium" size="sm">{s.name}</text>
        <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{hours(s.wh)>=24?(hours(s.wh)/24).toFixed(1)+" days":hours(s.wh).toFixed(1)+" hours"}</text>
      </row>
      <box background="surface-tertiary" height="9px" radius="full" clip>
        <box background={i===0?"#16836b":i===1?"#5085bc":"#9299a3"} width={`${s.wh/5040*100}%`} height="100%" radius="full"/>
      </box>
    </box>
  {/each}
  <caption>Estimates assume 85% usable battery energy through AC output, continuous equipment load, and no recharging. Actual runtime can be shorter, especially at very low loads due to inverter overhead.</caption>
</box>

## How to maximize aquarium survival time

For most aquariums, prioritize running the air pump and filter. Turn off unnecessary lighting and other nonessential equipment. Heating can be the biggest power drain, so monitor water temperature and avoid abrupt changes rather than automatically disconnecting a heater.

For an unattended aquarium, also check the power station's automatic switchover behavior and test whether the filter reliably restarts after an outage.

**Two questions so I can recommend the best power station for your actual aquarium:**

1. How big is your aquarium (10, 20, 55, 75, 125 gallons, etc.)?
2. Do you need to power **just the filter and air pump**, or **the heater too**?

Those two details can change the ideal purchase from a $200–$500 power station to a much larger backup system.
